items.criterion: Reports net sales of $23,276M vs consensus $23,050M: a beat of about $226M (+1.0%)
Reports core EPS $2.00 vs consensus $2.03 (miss of $0.03, -1.5%) and GAAP diluted EPS $1.97 vs $1.99
Characterises the quarter correctly as a sales beat with an EPS miss
Reports organic sales growth of 4.0% vs consensus 3.0% (beat)
Reports segment variances including Health Care net sales $3,318M vs $3,380M (miss, -1.8%) and at least one segment beat (Beauty +1.4% or Fabric & Home Care +1.0%)
All figures quoted from the release or consensus sheet match them exactly
A compact variance table is present and arithmetically correct
Explains the sales driver using the release: organic volume +2.4%, mix +1.1%, price +0.4%, FX neutral
Explains the gross margin miss: core gross margin 50.0% vs 50.8% consensus (-150 bp y/y), with commodities (-140 bp) as the main cause
Notes SG&A leverage as a partial offset (core SG&A down 80 bp to 24.1% of sales)
Reports core operating margin of 25.9% vs consensus 26.4% (-50 bp) and -80 bp y/y
Points out that the +1% EPS growth came with flat pre-tax earnings ($6,023M vs $6,034M) and a lower share count (2,407.2M vs 2,436.8M, about -1.2%), i.e. buyback support
Notes higher interest expense ($223M vs $197M) and/or lower non-operating income ($207M vs $268M)
Explains the core vs GAAP gap ($0.03 incremental restructuring)
States FY2027 guidance: organic growth 1% to 3% and core EPS $6.89 to $7.11 maintained; all-in sales growth 2% to 4% updated for Thorne
Compares guidance with consensus (core EPS midpoint $7.00 vs $7.04, about -0.6%) and concludes estimates are more likely to fall
Cites the cost headwinds: about $1.4B after-tax commodities and a combined $0.79 per share headwind
Gives a clear recommendation on whether the view or estimates change
Lists at least two specific items to watch next quarter (e.g., commodity costs, Thorne integration, volume, tariffs)
The memo fits on one page
The deliverable is a .docx or .pdf with a professional structure (header, table, short paragraphs) addressed to an investment committee
